title: Batman #1 Introduced Joker and Catwoman Without Featuring Them on Its Cover
excerpt:
The landmark 1940 comic launched two defining Batman relationships.
A graded copy has attracted a six-figure auction bid.
body_md:
One of the most influential superhero comics ever printed concealed its biggest historical surprise. Batman #1, published in 1940, featured the first appearances of both the Joker and the character who would become Catwoman, yet neither of those future icons appeared on its famous cover. The issue's importance has only grown across eight decades of comics, television and film.

The Joker's original story established a calculating, murderous criminal who publicly announced his intended victims and left them with terrifying smiles. Catwoman initially appeared as the Cat, a thief whose encounter with Batman introduced the fascination and moral tension that would define their relationship. The issue also featured Hugo Strange and arrived before Batman's later prohibition against killing was fully established.

Its legacy extends well beyond those debuts. The Joker and Catwoman have repeatedly reshaped Batman adaptations, from the 1960s television series to Tim Burton's films and modern reinterpretations. A CGC-graded copy of Batman #1 has reportedly reached a $140,000 bid at auction, underscoring the extraordinary value collectors place on this particular moment in superhero history.
